children.translated_text: In the seven-threaded rite of <s>Ananyaja</s>, acceptance of <s>anutarṣa</s> is absolutely necessary.
For, in awakening the bliss of lovemaking, it is the causal basis of indescribable bliss.
When the <s>udañjī</s> rises up, acceptance of the daughter of <s>Pracetas</s> is the supreme cause.
For it is impossible to perform the system of lovemaking when the person acted upon lacks the primary role of an agent.

children.text: prayojye narmavyāpāravistāre abhyutthānaviśiṣṭodañjyabhāve sarvāṅgīṇavyāpāropalakṣitaṃ ratitantraṃ kartum adhikārābhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: When an extensive amorous activity is to be performed, if there is no <s>udañjī</s> distinguished by erection, one is not qualified to perform the system of lovemaking characterized by activity involving the entire body.
In the sport of the system of lovemaking, accepting <s>sīdhu</s> (intoxicating liquor) is the supreme cause of the arising of indescribable pleasure.
In the playful sport of forming graceful, coquettish embraces, this is the innate nature of the daughter of the lord of <s>Puṣkara</s>.
A stream of honey, together with <s>Upaśyāmā</s>, produces boldness in the <s>udañjī</s>.
Entering together with <s>Śyāmā</s> is the supreme cause of retaining semen until the appointed limit marked by two watches of the night.
When a hairless sexual organ is penetrated, subsequent tasting by the woman is absolutely necessary.
While this subsequent tasting is performed, the pain of penetration is not experienced.

children.text: uttarasmin ghasre asaṃbheditam iva varāṅgaṃ paridṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: On the following day, the sexual organ appears as though it had not been penetrated.

children.text: kriyamāṇe narmavyāpāre udañjer dhārṣṭyasya phalegrahiḥ paridṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: When amorous activity is being performed, the fruitful boldness of the <s>udañjī</s> becomes apparent.

children.text: upaśyāmayā saha vyānatādibandhe samupasthitau pāśina ātmajāyāḥ svīkaraṇe anirvacanīyasukhānubhave hetuḥ kāraṇatvam ||
children.translated_text: When bindings such as <s>vyānata</s> are employed together with <s>Upaśyāmā</s>, acceptance of the daughter of <s>Pāśin</s> is the cause of experiencing indescribable pleasure.
In intercourse with girls who have not reached puberty, the purpose is accomplished by tasting only an atom-sized quantity.

children.text: tīyapratyayasya prakṛtibhūtāyām avasthāyāṃ kaśyasvīkaraṇasyātyāvaśyakatvaṃ sati pūrvarūpasaṃyoge ||
children.translated_text: In the condition that serves as the base of the suffix <s>-tīya</s>, acceptance of <s>kaśya</s> is absolutely necessary when there is conjunction with the prior form.
In the other condition, however, there is no qualification.
For in the one case there is no complete discernment.
And in the other, the constituent parts composed of the five elements are considerably weaker.
People who possess <s>Haripriyā</s> must necessarily follow this branch.
Engagement in this branch is not prescribed for others.
Consequently, by elimination, this teaching applies to those who are united with the ocean-born goddess.
On the day of a lineage descendant, acceptance of <s>anutarṣa</s> is absolutely necessary—so say <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> and others.
On days devoted to poetry it is most absolutely necessary—so say <s>Suratha</s> and the merchant.
For the two statements are assigned to those devoted to the worship of <s>Śakti</s>.
Others are to be instructed as the occasion demands.
For the second class, permission applies at all times.
For the first class, permission is granted according to the wording, on account of the sacrifice.

children.text: khaṇḍamaṇḍalādhipatyādīnām indirāvatāṃ janānām api sīdhugrahaṇasya vilāsaḥ sārvakālikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even for people who possess <s>Indirā</s>, such as rulers of territorial divisions and districts, the enjoyment of drinking <s>sīdhu</s> is permissible at all times.
Young women are permitted to do so when accompanied by their own beloved.
Even there, the prescription applies only in sacrifices to <s>Ananyaja</s>, not elsewhere.

children.text: yoṣāyāḥ āsyapadmena prāśanaṃ bhāṣāyāḥ prabodhe avyabhicaritakāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: Tasting with the lotus-mouth of a woman is an unfailing cause of the awakening of speech.

children.text: śyāmāyā āsyasahasrapattrād anuprāśanam aparokṣānubhavena mūlaprakṛteḥ svarūpasyānudarśanam ||
children.translated_text: Subsequent tasting from the thousand-petaled mouth of <s>Śyāmā</s> is, through direct experience, a manifestation of the essential form of primordial nature.
